# # Dependency Trace: TLS Certificate Verification from git through curl to OpenSSL

## Context

When `git clone` fails with a TLS certificate error, the error actually
originates in OpenSSL, passes through libcurl, and is reported by git. The
full verification chain crosses three codebases, each with its own
configuration points that affect certificate trust decisions.

Understanding this chain is critical for diagnosing corporate proxy/CA issues
where custom certificates need to be trusted.

## Task

Trace the TLS certificate verification path from git's HTTPS transport through
curl's OpenSSL backend to OpenSSL's X509 verification, documenting every
configuration point.

## Repos in Workspace

- `/workspace/git/` -- git v2.41.0 (consumer)
- `/workspace/curl/` -- curl 8.1.2 (intermediary)
- `/workspace/openssl/` -- OpenSSL 3.1.1 (upstream TLS library)

## Expected Output

Write `/workspace/DEPENDENCY_TRACE.md` containing:

1. Git's SSL configuration entry points (http.sslCAInfo, http.sslVerify, env vars)
2. How git configures curl for TLS (curl_easy_setopt calls)
3. Curl's OpenSSL backend integration (vtls/openssl.c)
4. OpenSSL's X509 certificate chain verification code path
5. All configuration knobs across the three repos that affect verification


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1, github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2, github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0

The markdown content is fully composed below. Since the workspace file system isn't directly writable via these tools, here is the complete `/workspace/DEPENDENCY_TRACE.md` content, sourced directly from the three repos:

# Dependency Trace: TLS Certificate Verification — git → curl → OpenSSL

**Sources:**
- [`github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0) — `http.c`
- [`github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2) — `lib/vtls/openssl.c`
- [`github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1) — `crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c`, `ssl/ssl_lib.c`

---

## 1. Git's SSL Configuration Entry Points

All SSL config is read and stored in [`http.c`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c).

### 1.1 Static Variables ([http.c L41–71](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L41-71))

```c
static int curl_ssl_verify = -1;   // -1 = unset; resolved to 1 at init time
static const char *ssl_cainfo;     // maps to http.sslCAInfo
static const char *ssl_capath;     // maps to http.sslCAPath
static const char *ssl_cert;
static const char *ssl_key;
static const char *ssl_cipherlist;
static const char *ssl_version;
static const char *ssl_pinnedkey;  // maps to http.pinnedPubkey
static const char *http_proxy_ssl_ca_info;
```

### 1.2 `git config` Keys — parsed in `http_options()` ([http.c L366–413](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L366-413))

| Config Key | Variable | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `http.sslVerify` | `curl_ssl_verify` | Master on/off for peer cert verification |
| `http.sslCAInfo` | `ssl_cainfo` | Path to CA bundle PEM file |
| `http.sslCAPath` | `ssl_capath` | Directory of hashed CA certs |
| `http.sslCert` | `ssl_cert` | Client certificate file |
| `http.sslCertType` | `ssl_cert_type` | Client cert type (`PEM`/`DER`) |
| `http.sslKey` | `ssl_key` | Client private key |
| `http.sslKeyType` | `ssl_key_type` | Key type |
| `http.sslCipherList` | `ssl_cipherlist` | OpenSSL cipher string |
| `http.sslVersion` | `ssl_version` | Minimum TLS version (`tlsv1.2`, etc.) |
| `http.sslBackend` | `http_ssl_backend` | Backend name (`openssl`, `schannel`) |
| `http.pinnedPubkey` | `ssl_pinnedkey` | Public key hash pinning |
| `http.sslTry` | `curl_ssl_try` | Opportunistic SSL (`CURLUSESSL_TRY`) |
| `http.schannelCheckRevoke` | `http_schannel_check_revoke` | CRL check on Windows |
| `http.schannelUseSslCaInfo` | `http_schannel_use_ssl_cainfo` | Force CAInfo on schannel backend |

### 1.3 Environment Variables — applied in `http_init()` ([http.c L1263–1304](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L1263-1304))

| Env Var | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` | Sets `curl_ssl_verify = 0`; disables all cert verification |
| `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` | Overrides `http.sslCAInfo` |
| `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` | Overrides `http.sslCAPath` |
| `GIT_SSL_CERT` | Client certificate file |
| `GIT_SSL_CERT_TYPE` | Client cert type |
| `GIT_SSL_KEY` | Client private key |
| `GIT_SSL_KEY_TYPE` | Key type |
| `GIT_SSL_VERSION` | Minimum TLS version |
| `GIT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST` | Cipher suite restriction |
| `GIT_PROXY_SSL_CAINFO` | CA bundle for HTTPS proxy |
| `GIT_PROXY_SSL_CERT` | Client cert for HTTPS proxy |
| `GIT_PROXY_SSL_KEY` | Client key for HTTPS proxy |

**Priority:** Env vars are applied in `http_init()` and shadow any `git config` values. `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` is especially absolute — it unconditionally sets `curl_ssl_verify = 0` regardless of config. Default: if `curl_ssl_verify` is still `-1` after all processing, it is set to `1` ([L1282–1283](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L1282-1283)).

---

## 2. How Git Configures curl for TLS

The CURL handle is built in `get_curl_handle()` ([http.c L943–1098](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L943-1098)); the global default is created by `http_init()` at [L1307](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L1307).

### 2.1 Verification On/Off ([L950–958](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L950-958))

```c
if (!curl_ssl_verify) {
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 0);
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 0);
} else {
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1);
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2); // strict hostname match
}
```

### 2.2 CA Bundle / CA Path ([L1039–1052](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/git--v2.41.0/-/blob/http.c?L1039-1052))

```c
// schannel backend: clear CAInfo → use Windows certificate store
if (http_ssl_backend && !strcmp("schannel", http_ssl_backend) &&
    !http_schannel_use_ssl_cainfo) {
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_CAINFO, NULL);
} else if (ssl_cainfo != NULL || http_proxy_ssl_ca_info != NULL) {
    if (ssl_cainfo)
        curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_CAINFO, ssl_cainfo);
    if (http_proxy_ssl_ca_info)
        curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_PROXY_CAINFO, http_proxy_ssl_ca_info);
}
if (ssl_capath)
    curl_easy_setopt(result, CURLOPT_CAPATH, ssl_capath);
```

### 2.3 Complete `curl_easy_setopt` Inventory

| `CURLOPT_*` | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SSL_VERIFYPEER` | L951/L955 | Enable/disable CA chain verification |
| `SSL_VERIFYHOST` | L952/L957 | 0=none, 2=strict hostname check |
| `CAINFO` | L1047 | CA bundle file (PEM) |
| `CAPATH` | L1034 | CA directory (hashed PEM) |
| `PROXY_CAINFO` | L1050 | CA bundle for HTTPS proxy |
| `SSLCERT` | L1024 | Client certificate |
| `SSLCERTTYPE` | L1026 | Client cert type |
| `SSLKEY` | L1030 | Client private key |
| `SSLKEYTYPE` | L1032 | Key type |
| `KEYPASSWD` | L1028 | Password for encrypted key |
| `PINNEDPUBLICKEY` | L1037 | SHA-256 pinned public key |
| `SSLVERSION` | L1007 | Minimum TLS version |
| `SSL_CIPHER_LIST` | L1020 | OpenSSL cipher string |
| `SSL_OPTIONS` | L992 | Flags e.g. `CURLSSLOPT_NO_REVOKE` |
| `USE_SSL` | L1098 | `CURLUSESSL_TRY` for opportunistic TLS |

## 3. curl's OpenSSL Backend Integration (`lib/vtls/openssl.c`)

### 3.1 Entry Point: `ossl_connect_step1()` ([L3405](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3405))

Called by curl's connection layer when establishing HTTPS. Sequence:
1. Creates `SSL_CTX` via `SSL_CTX_new(TLS_client_method())` ([L3480](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3480))
2. Sets TLS version range, SSL options (`SSL_OP_ALL`, etc.)
3. Calls `Curl_ssl_setup_x509_store()` to populate CA trust store
4. Sets verify mode via `SSL_CTX_set_verify()` ([L3688](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3688))
5. Fires optional `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` callback ([L3708](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3708))
6. Creates `SSL *` and begins handshake

### 3.2 Verify Mode ([L3684–3689](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3684-3689))

```c
/* OpenSSL always tries to verify the peer; this only says whether it should
 * FAIL to connect if verification fails, or continue anyway (result checked
 * with SSL_get_verify_result() below). */
SSL_CTX_set_verify(backend->ctx,
                   verifypeer ? SSL_VERIFY_PEER : SSL_VERIFY_NONE, NULL);
```

With `SSL_VERIFY_NONE`, OpenSSL still performs verification but does not abort the handshake on failure. curl then explicitly checks `SSL_get_verify_result()` post-handshake.

### 3.3 `Curl_ssl_setup_x509_store()` ([L3359–3403](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3359-3403))

Decides whether to reuse a cached `X509_STORE` (keyed on CAfile path) or call `populate_x509_store()`. Caching is eligible only when `CURLOPT_CAINFO` is the sole CA source.

### 3.4 `populate_x509_store()` — CA Loading ([L3000–3272](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3000-3272))

| Step | Code | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Windows native CA store | `CertOpenSystemStore` → `X509_STORE_add_cert()` | `ssl_config->native_ca_store` |
| In-memory CA blob | `load_cacert_from_memory()` | `CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB` set; **overrides** `CURLOPT_CAINFO` |
| CA file (OpenSSL ≥ 3.0) | `X509_STORE_load_file(store, ssl_cafile)` | `CURLOPT_CAINFO` set |
| CA directory (OpenSSL ≥ 3.0) | `X509_STORE_load_path(store, ssl_capath)` | `CURLOPT_CAPATH` set |
| Legacy file+dir (OpenSSL < 3.0) | `X509_STORE_load_locations()` | |
| Built-in fallback | `X509_STORE_set_default_paths()` | No other source, `CURL_CA_FALLBACK` defined |
| CRL file | `X509_load_crl_file()` + `X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL` | `CURLOPT_CRLFILE` set |
| Store flags | `X509_V_FLAG_TRUSTED_FIRST`, `X509_V_FLAG_PARTIAL_CHAIN` | Always when `verifypeer` |

`X509_V_FLAG_TRUSTED_FIRST` ([L3255](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3255)) causes OpenSSL to prefer trust-store issuers, avoiding problems with server-sent legacy intermediates. `X509_V_FLAG_PARTIAL_CHAIN` ([L3267](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L3267)) allows intermediate CAs in the trust store to act as trust anchors.

### 3.5 Post-Handshake Checks ([L4066–4200](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L4066-4200))

After `SSL_connect()`:
1. `SSL_get1_peer_certificate()` — fail if no cert ([L4066](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L4066))
2. `ossl_verifyhost()` — CN/SAN hostname match if `verifyhost` ([L4101](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L4101))
3. `X509_check_issued()` — issuer pinning if `CURLOPT_ISSUERCERT` ([L4175](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/curl--curl-8_1_2/-/blob/lib/vtls/openssl.c?L4175))
4. `SSL_get_verify_result()` — chain result check; non-`X509_V_OK` → `CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION`

---

## 4. OpenSSL's X509 Certificate Chain Verification (`crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c`)

### 4.1 `X509_verify_cert()` — Top Level ([L261–305](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L261-305))

```c
int X509_verify_cert(X509_STORE_CTX *ctx) {
    // Guards: ctx/cert non-null, chain not reused
    ossl_x509_add_cert_new(&ctx->chain, ctx->cert, X509_ADD_FLAG_UP_REF);
    ctx->num_untrusted = 1;
    CB_FAIL_IF(!check_key_level(ctx, ctx->cert), ..., X509_V_ERR_EE_KEY_TOO_SMALL);
    ret = DANETLS_ENABLED(ctx->dane) ? dane_verify(ctx) : verify_chain(ctx);
}
```

Called internally by OpenSSL during `SSL_connect()`; not called directly by curl.

### 4.2 `verify_chain()` — Orchestration ([L211–248](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L211-248))

```c
static int verify_chain(X509_STORE_CTX *ctx) {
    if ((ok = build_chain(ctx))          <= 0) return ok;  // build cert chain
    if ((ok = check_extensions(ctx))     <= 0) return ok;  // X.509 v3 extensions
    if ((ok = check_auth_level(ctx))     <= 0) return ok;  // min security level
    if ((ok = check_id(ctx))             <= 0) return ok;  // subject identity
    if ((ok = X509_get_pubkey_parameters(...)) <= 0) return ok; // key params
    if ((ok = ctx->check_revocation(ctx))<= 0) return ok;  // CRL/OCSP
    // Suite B compliance
    ok = ctx->verify ? ctx->verify(ctx) : internal_verify(ctx); // signatures + expiry
    if ((ok = check_name_constraints(ctx)) <= 0) return ok;
    // RFC 3779, policy check
}
```

### 4.3 `build_chain()` ([L2988](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L2988))

Walks from leaf toward trust anchor. Search policy flags:
- `S_DOUNTRUSTED` — search server-sent intermediates first
- `S_DOTRUSTED` — search the `X509_STORE` (populated by curl from CAfile/CApath)
- `S_DOALTERNATE` — retry with alternate chain if first attempt fails

Controlled by `X509_V_FLAG_TRUSTED_FIRST` (prefer store first) and `X509_V_FLAG_NO_ALT_CHAINS`. Stops at `max_depth = ctx->param->depth + 1`. Trust is established when `ctx->get_issuer()` → `X509_STORE_CTX_get1_issuer()` finds a cert in the `X509_STORE`.

### 4.4 `check_extensions()` ([L451–600](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L451-600))

Validates RFC 5280 X.509 v3 extensions per cert in chain:
- Basic Constraints: `CA:TRUE` required for intermediate certs
- Key Usage: `keyCertSign` required on CA certs
- Extended Key Usage: purpose check (e.g. `serverAuth`)
- Proxy certificate policy
- With `X509_V_FLAG_X509_STRICT`: strict non-empty subject/issuer, SAN rules, signature algorithm consistency

### 4.5 `internal_verify()` ([L1743–1850](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L1743-1850))

Walks the chain top-down. For each issuer/subject pair:
1. `ossl_x509_signing_allowed()` — checks key usage permits signing
2. `X509_verify(xs, pkey)` — verifies subject cert's cryptographic signature against issuer's public key ([L1823](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L1823))
3. `ossl_x509_check_cert_time()` — checks NotBefore/NotAfter ([L1830](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c?L1830))
4. `ctx->verify_cb(1, ctx)` — application verify callback fires at each depth; can override errors

### 4.6 OpenSSL Trust Store Loading (`ssl/ssl_lib.c` [L4362–4450](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/openssl--openssl-3.1.1/-/blob/ssl/ssl_lib.c?L4362-4450))

```c
SSL_CTX_set_default_verify_paths(ctx)        // reads SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR env vars
SSL_CTX_load_verify_file(ctx, CAfile)        // PEM bundle file → X509_STORE_load_file_ex
SSL_CTX_load_verify_dir(ctx, CApath)         // hashed dir    → X509_STORE_load_path
SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations(ctx, f, d)     // legacy combined API (OpenSSL < 3.0 compat)
```

## 5. All Configuration Knobs Affecting Verification

### 5.1 Git Layer

| Knob | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `http.sslVerify` | git config | Master on/off |
| `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` | env | Forces verify=0 (overrides config) |
| `http.sslCAInfo` / `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` | path | CA bundle file |
| `http.sslCAPath` / `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` | path | CA directory |
| `http.sslCert` / `GIT_SSL_CERT` | path | Client cert |
| `http.sslKey` / `GIT_SSL_KEY` | path | Client key |
| `http.sslCipherList` / `GIT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST` | string | Cipher restriction |
| `http.sslVersion` / `GIT_SSL_VERSION` | string | Min TLS version |
| `http.pinnedPubkey` | hash | Public key pinning |
| `http.sslBackend` | string | Backend (`openssl`/`schannel`) |
| `http.schannelCheckRevoke` | bool | CRL check (Windows) |
| `http.schannelUseSslCaInfo` | bool | Force CAInfo on schannel |
| `GIT_PROXY_SSL_CAINFO` | env | CA bundle for HTTPS proxy |

### 5.2 curl Layer

| CURLOPT | Effect |
|---|---|
| `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` | 0=skip chain verification, 1=verify |
| `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` | 0=none, 2=strict hostname |
| `CURLOPT_CAINFO` | CA bundle file (PEM) |
| `CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB` | CA bundle in memory; **overrides** `CAINFO` |
| `CURLOPT_CAPATH` | CA directory (hashed PEM files) |
| `CURLOPT_PROXY_CAINFO` | CA bundle for HTTPS proxy |
| `CURLOPT_CRLFILE` | CRL file; enables `X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL` |
| `CURLOPT_ISSUERCERT` | Pin exact issuer certificate |
| `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` | Expected public key (file or `sha256//...`) |
| `CURLOPT_SSLVERSION` | Minimum TLS version |
| `CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST` | OpenSSL cipher string |
| `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` | Callback for direct `SSL_CTX *` manipulation |
| `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS` | `CURLSSLOPT_NO_REVOKE`, `CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA` |
| `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` env | curl default CA bundle path |

Internal flags in `ssl_config`:
- `native_ca_store` — import OS native CA (Windows)
- `no_partialchain` — disable `X509_V_FLAG_PARTIAL_CHAIN`
- `ca_cache_timeout` — `X509_STORE` reuse lifetime

### 5.3 OpenSSL Layer

| Knob | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `SSL_CERT_FILE` | env | Default CA bundle file |
| `SSL_CERT_DIR` | env | Default CA directory |
| `OPENSSL_CONF` | env | OpenSSL config file location |
| `X509_V_FLAG_TRUSTED_FIRST` | store flag | Prefer trust store over server-sent chain |
| `X509_V_FLAG_PARTIAL_CHAIN` | store flag | Allow intermediate CAs as trust anchors |
| `X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK` | store flag | CRL check for leaf cert |
| `X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL` | store flag | CRL check for all chain certs |
| `X509_V_FLAG_NO_ALT_CHAINS` | store flag | Disable alternate chain search |
| `X509_V_FLAG_X509_STRICT` | store flag | Strict RFC 5280 extension checking |
| `X509_V_FLAG_POLICY_CHECK` | store flag | Enforce certificate policy |
| `X509_V_FLAG_CHECK_SS_SIGNATURE` | store flag | Verify self-signed cert signature |
| `ctx->param->depth` | verify param | Maximum chain depth |
| `ctx->param->purpose` | verify param | Expected purpose (e.g. `SSL_server`) |
| `ctx->verify_cb` | function ptr | Application verify error override |
| `ctx->check_revocation` | function ptr | Pluggable revocation checking |

## 6. End-to-End Call Flow

```
git clone https://example.com/repo.git
  │
  ├─ git/http.c: git_config(http_options)    ← reads http.ssl* from .gitconfig / .git/config
  ├─ git/http.c: http_init()                 ← reads GIT_SSL_* env vars (override config)
  │    └─ curl_ssl_verify defaults to 1 if unset
  │
  ├─ git/http.c: get_curl_handle()
  │    ├─ curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1)
  │    ├─ curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2)
  │    ├─ curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_CAINFO, ssl_cainfo)    ← from http.sslCAInfo
  │    ├─ curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_CAPATH, ssl_capath)    ← from http.sslCAPath
  │    └─ ... (cipher, version, client cert, pinning)
  │
  ├─ curl: curl_easy_perform()
  │    └─ lib/vtls/openssl.c: ossl_connect_step1()
  │         ├─ SSL_CTX_new(TLS_client_method())
  │         ├─ Curl_ssl_setup_x509_store()
  │         │    └─ populate_x509_store()
  │         │         ├─ [Windows]  CertOpenSystemStore → X509_STORE_add_cert()
  │         │         ├─ [blob]     load_cacert_from_memory()     ← CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB
  │         │         ├─ [file]     X509_STORE_load_file()        ← CURLOPT_CAINFO
  │         │         ├─ [dir]      X509_STORE_load_path()        ← CURLOPT_CAPATH
  │         │         ├─ [fallback] X509_STORE_set_default_paths() (reads SSL_CERT_FILE)
  │         │         ├─ [CRL]      X509_load_crl_file() + X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL
  │         │         └─ X509_STORE_set_flags(TRUSTED_FIRST | PARTIAL_CHAIN)
  │         ├─ SSL_CTX_set_verify(ctx, SSL_VERIFY_PEER, NULL)
  │         ├─ [CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION callback — app can inject custom CAs here]
  │         └─ SSL_connect()      ← TLS handshake
  │
  └─ OpenSSL: TLS handshake (ssl/ssl_cert.c → x509_vfy.c)
```

## 7. Corporate CA / Proxy Diagnosis

| Error | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `unable to get local issuer certificate` | Corporate CA not in trust store | `git config http.sslCAInfo /path/to/corp-ca-bundle.pem` or `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` |
| `certificate verify failed` | Same, or cert expired | Check CAInfo path; verify cert validity dates |
| `no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name` | MITM proxy presents wrong CN | Add proxy's CA to CAInfo; or configure proxy correctly |
| `CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE` | CAfile not readable / wrong format | Check path and PEM encoding |
| Proxy intercepts HTTPS | MITM proxy with own CA | Set `GIT_PROXY_SSL_CAINFO` with proxy CA bundle |

Bypass (debug only — insecure):
```sh
GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=1 git clone https://...
# or
git -c http.sslVerify=false clone https://...
```
